_about: PLACEHOLDER conversations, to show how talking and choices work until the real storylines are written. A line is [speaker id, text]; 'you' is the player. Choices can have conditions (if) and change things (effects: bond, money, setFlag). {name} is the player's name and {currency} the money's name.

lines: There you are, {name}. Did you sleep well?

choices.text: Yes! I dreamed I could fly.
Not really. The dog next door barked all night.
Can I go outside to play?

lines: Fly? Then you can fly to the shop for me one day.
Go on, the morning is the best part of the day.
That dog. I'll have a word with Mrs Pell.
Go and get some air. It'll wake you up.
Already? You haven't even said good morning.
Fine. Stay on Willow Lane, and be back before dark.
Mum... Mr Ambrose has new sweets at the shop.
And you have your own {currency}, don't you?

choices.text: I want to keep mine. Can you buy them?
I'll use my own. Just checking.
Can I earn some? I can sweep the yard.

lines: Keep yours, spend mine? Nice try.
Good. It's yours. Spend it how you like, but it won't come back.
Sweep it properly and there's 5 {currency} in it for you.
Back before dark, {name}. I mean it.
Hey. You live at the end of the lane, right? I'm Nico.

choices.text: I bet I can run faster than you.

lines: Yes! Nobody else on this street is our age. It's all old people and cats.
You don't talk much. That's okay. I talk enough for two.
No way. I'm the fastest on Willow Lane.
Tomorrow. Bench to the lamp post. You're on.
Mr Ambrose has new sweets. The fizzy ones.
One day I'll have a shop like his. Then sweets are free. For me.
Did you see that cat? It's been sitting on the car all day.
Oh, hello dear. You're the little one from the end house.
My knees aren't what they were. Would you carry my bag to the door?
What a kind child. Your mother raised you well.
Here. Don't tell her I gave you this.
Busy. At your age. Well, off you go then.
The lane was all fields when I was your age. Fields, dear.
Welcome, welcome. What can I get you?
Good choice. Careful, they make your eyes water.
Looking is free. Buying is how I eat.
